title: Nursing Note - Day Shift Assessment
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Day shift head-to-toe assessment after bedside report; resuscitation complete, albumin infusing, feeds at goal.
body:
**Report**
Bedside report received 06:45-07:00 from E. Haddad, RN. Overnight: Parkland resuscitation completed at 01:30 (LR now 75 mL/h with albumin 5% 500 mL running 06:00-10:00). Insulin infusion running since 00:30. Lorazepam 1 mg IV x1 at 03:00 for agitation with the ETT; hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV at 05:45. Tube feeds reached goal 70 mL/h at 06:00. FiO2 weaned to 0.40 at 04:00. Allergies: NKDA. Full Code. Contact precautions (burn unit).

**Neuro**
RASS -2 (goal -1 to -2 today), CPOT 1/8. Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h. Pupils 3 mm, brisk and equal. Opens eyes to voice. Soft left wrist restraint on, skin under restraint intact.

**Cardiovascular**
HR 96 sinus, BP 111/64 (MAP 80) by left radial arterial line, T 99.4 F (bladder). Transducer leveled and zeroed at the phlebostatic axis at start of shift, pressure bag 300 mmHg, waveform crisp. Right arm elevated on pillows in position of function, hand splinted. Doppler signals present at the right hand, cap refill under 3 seconds in the fingertips, no increase in forearm tension; escharotomy incisions dressed.

**Respiratory**
AC/VC VT 450, set RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.40. PIP 24 / Pplat 17, SpO2 98%, RR 17. ETT 8.0 at 24 cm at the teeth, secured, HOB above 30 degrees. Breath sounds coarse bilaterally, small thin tan secretions on suction. ABG 06:00: pH 7.41, PaCO2 40, PaO2 124, HCO3 25, lactate 1.4.

**GI / Nutrition**
OG tube 16 Fr: Osmolite 1.5 at 70 mL/h, free water 30 mL q4h. Abdomen soft, non-distended, bowel sounds present. Bladder pressures q6h have stayed in the 10-14 mmHg range.

**GU / Renal**
Foley to gravity, clear amber urine. UOP 45 mL (0500-0600) and 47 mL (0600-0700) = 0.57 mL/kg/h.

**Labs (06:00)**
Na 134, K 3.9, Cl 108, CO2 24, BUN 23, Cr 1.1, glucose 177, Ca 7.7 (iCa 1.02), Mg 1.6 (low), Phos 2.1 (low). Albumin 2.6 and INR 1.2 (05:00); prealbumin 7.1; triglycerides 168 on propofol. Low Mg/Phos to be rechecked with noon labs.

**Endocrine**
Insulin infusion 1.5 units/h. POC glucose 182 (05:30), 179 (06:30), 170 (07:30).

**Skin / Wounds / Lines**
Chest and right arm dressings dry and intact with scant serosanguineous strike-through. Face with bacitracin. Low air-loss mattress, turn q2h off the burned side. Left IJ triple lumen day 2, dressing clean/dry/intact; left AC 18 g PIV patent; left radial A-line; Foley; OG.

**Plan**
SAT at 08:00; dressing change at 14:00 with N. Ibarra, RN; hourly neuro-vascular checks of the right hand; labs at noon.

title: Nursing Note - Daily Sedation Interruption
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: SAT performed at 08:00; patient awake and following commands; no SBT today.
body:
**Sedation interruption (SAT) 08:00**
Per order, propofol paused at 08:00 with RN at bedside; fentanyl continued at 100 mcg/h for analgesia. Pre-SAT: RASS -2, CPOT 1/8, HR 92, BP 110/65 (MAP 80), SpO2 98%, T 99.4 F.

**Response**
- Awoke to voice within minutes; RASS 0, calm, eyes tracking the room.
- Follows commands with the LEFT hand (squeezes, wiggles fingers, thumbs up) and moves the left leg on request; right hand splinted, fingers pink with brisk cap refill.
- Mouthed "mom" and became tearful. Mother Linda Delaney was at bedside and spoke to him; he calmed and held her hand. Reoriented to place and reason for ICU stay by nodding to simple questions.
- CPOT 1-2/8 during the interruption (mild grimace with repositioning only); no hydromorphone needed.
- Hemodynamics stable throughout: HR 92-98, MAP 78-82, SpO2 98%, RR 17-18 on AC/VC; no ventilator dyssynchrony, no coughing/bucking against the tube.
- Pulled gently against the left wrist restraint once; redirected, restraint maintained for ETT/line protection, circulation intact.
- CAM-ICU negative (RASS 0, attentive, follows commands, no disorganized thinking).

**Restart**
Propofol restarted at 08:35 at 20 mcg/kg/min (half the prior 30). RASS settled at -1 to -2. Plan to increase to 30 mcg/kg/min at 09:30 if RASS stays within the -1 to -2 goal and comfort allows; titrate by RASS and CPOT.

**SBT**
No spontaneous breathing trial today. Patient is still in the active post-resuscitation fluid-shift phase with albumin 5% infusing until 10:00, FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5, and burn team/intensivist plan is to reassess for extubation tomorrow after the dressing and sepsis surveillance; discussed with RT D. Alvarez, RRT.

**Family**
Linda updated on how well he woke up; she was tearful and relieved. Explained that the tube and sedation are still needed today.

**Plan**
Continue hourly RASS/CPOT, CAM-ICU each shift, oral care, HOB above 30 degrees, left-hand neuro checks, pre-medicate for the 14:00 dressing change.

title: Nursing Note - Midmorning Update
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Midmorning assessment update covering meds, glucose/insulin, urine output, mobility and family.
body:
**Hemodynamics / Respiratory**
09:00-10:00: HR 95-96, BP 111/63 (MAP 79), RR 17-18, SpO2 98%, T 99.5 F. FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5, PIP 25 / Pplat 18. Albumin 5% 500 mL finished at 10:00 without reaction; LR increased from 75 to 100 mL/h at 10:00 per order. RASS -2, CPOT 1/8 on propofol and fentanyl 100 mcg/h.

**Medications given 09:00**
Pantoprazole 40 mg IV (stress ulcer prophylaxis), chlorhexidine 0.12% oral rinse 15 mL, ascorbic acid 500 mg, zinc sulfate 220 mg, multivitamin with minerals, thiamine 100 mg / folic acid 1 mg per OG, senna-docusate 2 tablets per OG, bacitracin to face. Heparin 5,000 units nebulized 07:00 and albuterol neb 08:00 given. Heparin SQ due 14:00.

**Glucose / Insulin**
Hourly POC: 170 (07:30), 169 (08:30), 175 (09:30), 173 (10:30). Insulin infusion at 1.5 units/h, goal 140-180; no rate change required.

**Nutrition**
Osmolite 1.5 at goal 70 mL/h, residual checks q4h under 500 mL, no emesis. Free water flushes continue.

**I&O**
UOP 46 (0700-0800), 48 (0800-0900), 48 mL (0900-1000) = 0.56-0.59 mL/kg/h, goal 30-50 mL/h. Intake 338, 308, 308 mL per hour including albumin and feeds.

**Mobility / Therapy**
PT (S. Kim, PT) and OT (H. Larsen, OTR/L) consulted but not started yet; deferred until after the dressing change and while on bedrest with the HOB up. Passive ROM to the left arm and both legs done with turning; right hand kept elevated and splinted; right-hand Doppler signals present, fingertips warm with brisk cap refill.

**Family**
Linda Delaney remains at bedside and helped with a short mouth-care routine under supervision. Jenna Whitaker called for an update; I reviewed his morning wake-up and the plan for the dressing change. Child life/social work (K. Abara, LCSW) offered for Ava; family will think about a short visit.

**Plan**
Noon labs, replacement per results, dressing change at 14:00 with N. Ibarra, RN, hydromorphone 15 minutes prior, continue hourly checks.

title: Nursing Note - Electrolyte Replacement
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Low K/Mg/Phos on 12:00 labs; replacement ordered and started.
body:
**Labs (12:00)**
- K 3.6 (down from 3.9 at 06:00); Mg 1.7; Phos 2.1 (low); Ca 7.6 (low); Na 135; Cr 1.1; BUN 25; glucose 175.
- CBC: WBC 15.4, Hgb 11.8, Hct 35.4, platelets 196. CK 410 (down from 840).
Low Phos had been noted on the 06:00 panel (Mg 1.6, Phos 2.1) and was flagged to Dr. Brandt's team; repletion ordered after the noon recheck.

**Orders and administration**
- Potassium chloride 20 mEq in 100 mL via central line over 2 h started 12:30; second 20 mEq dose due 14:30.
- Magnesium sulfate 2 g in 50 mL over 1 h due 13:30.
- Sodium phosphate 15 mmol in 250 mL over 4 h due 15:00.
Infusions to run on separate pumps via the left IJ; verified with a second RN and with pharmacy (A. Chen, PharmD) that doses and rates match the orders. Repeat BMP/Mg/Phos with the evening labs.

**Monitoring**
Telemetry: sinus rhythm 97 bpm, no ectopy, no new ST or T-wave changes while K is low. BP 110/62 (MAP 78), RR 17, SpO2 97%, T 99.7 F. Central line site clean, dry, intact, no infiltration or pain with potassium.

**Insulin / glucose**
Insulin infusion reduced to 1 unit/h at 12:00 per protocol; POC glucose 173 (11:30), 174 (12:30). Insulin shifts K and Phos intracellularly, so levels will be followed closely.

**Other**
UOP 46 mL (1100-1200), 0.56 mL/kg/h. Feeds 70 mL/h, no residual issues. RASS -2, CPOT 1/8. Will assess for muscle weakness and ectopy, and hold potassium for any urine output under 30 mL/h for 2 consecutive hours.

**Plan**
Finish K, Mg, Phos replacement, then recheck. Dressing change at 14:00.

title: Nursing Note - Burn Dressing Change Findings
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Dressing change with N. Ibarra, RN showed new signs of wound infection; fever trend noted.
body:
**Pre-medication / pain**
Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV given at 13:45, 15 minutes before the 14:00 dressing change. CPOT was 2/8 at 13:00 and rose to 5/8 during dressing removal at 14:00. Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min and fentanyl 100 mcg/h continued; RASS -2.

**Dressing change 14:00 with N. Ibarra, RN (burn nurse specialist)**
Full sterile technique, gown/mask/gloves. Findings that are NEW since yesterday:
- Purulent drainage on the chest and right arm dressings.
- Foul odor at the wound bed.
- Spreading erythema beyond the original burn margin on the right anterior chest.
- Eschar separating with a dark violaceous area at the right chest border.
- Increased pain response to cleansing (CPOT 5/8).
Right hand: Doppler signals present, fingers warm. Face: superficial, bacitracin applied. Silver sulfadiazine 1% reapplied to chest and right arm per current order. Margin of erythema to be marked with skin marker at 14:30 and photographed/measured by N. Ibarra.

**Vital sign trend**
- 13:00: T 99.9 F, HR 97, BP 109/61 (MAP 77), RR 18
- 14:00: T 100.4 F, HR 105, BP 106/55 (MAP 72), RR 20, SpO2 98%
Temperature up from 99.4 F this morning; HR up from the low 90s. Acetaminophen 1,000 mg IV and heparin SQ given at 14:00.

**Other data**
ABG 14:00: pH 7.40, PaCO2 41, PaO2 118, HCO3 25. UOP 45 (1200-1300) and 41 mL (1300-1400). POC glucose 177 at 13:30. Mg 2 g infused 13:30; KCl 20 mEq 2nd dose due 14:30; K 3.6 at noon.

**Communication**
Findings reported verbally to N. Ibarra, RN at the bedside. Plan: recheck temperature and perfusion at 15:00; if fever continues or HR/MAP trend worsens, I will call Dr. Okafor and Dr. Brandt with an SBAR.

**Plan**
Continue hourly vitals, watch UOP, CPOT before further wound care, keep right arm elevated.

title: Nursing Note - Sepsis SBAR
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: SBAR notification of surgeon and intensivist for fever, tachycardia and falling urine output with infected wound.
body:
**S (Situation)**
Suspected burn wound sepsis. At 15:30 T 101.1 F, HR 113, BP 105/51 (MAP 69), RR 23, SpO2 96% on the ventilator. Called Dr. Okafor (burn surgery) and Dr. Brandt (critical care) at 15:40.

**B (Background)**
34 y/o male, 22% TBSA flame burn with inhalation injury, hospital day 2, intubated. Wound change at 14:00 dressing change with N. Ibarra: new purulent drainage, foul odor, spreading erythema beyond the burn margin, eschar separation with dark violaceous area at the right chest border. NKDA, Full Code.

**A (Assessment)**
- Trend: T 99.9 (13:00), 100.4 (14:00), 100.9 (15:00), 101.1 (15:30). HR 97, 105, 108, 113. MAP 77, 72, 71, 69. RR 18 to 23.
- UOP falling: 45 (1200-1300), 41 (1300-1400), 36 mL (1400-1500) = 0.44 mL/kg/h and trending down.
- POC glucose 205 at 15:30 (was 173 this morning); insulin infusion raised to 1.5 units/h at 15:00.
- Pain CPOT 4/8; RASS -2. Skin warm, fingertips with brisk cap refill. Last WBC 15.4, lactate 1.4 (06:00), K 3.6.
I am concerned this is early sepsis from the wound infection.

**R (Recommendation / orders received)**
Dr. Okafor and Dr. Brandt acknowledged and gave orders:
- Cultures x4 sites before antibiotics: wound swab from area of drainage, blood x2 (peripheral and central line), tracheal aspirate, urine from Foley.
- Lactate, procalcitonin, CBC with differential, coags.
- Broad-spectrum antibiotics after cultures; pharmacy to dose.
- Dr. Okafor to examine the wound at the bedside; further orders to follow.

**Actions**
Cultures being collected at 15:50 with sterile technique. Antibiotic orders being verified with A. Chen, PharmD. Hourly vitals, strict I&O, and Foley output continue. Sepsis screen documented. Mother Linda informed that a fever and a possible infection are being treated.

**Plan**
Draw lactate/PCT/CBC immediately after cultures, give antibiotics within 1 hour, track MAP goal 65 or higher and UOP 0.5 mL/kg/h, call for MAP under 65, UOP under 30 mL/h, or any worsening.

title: Nursing Note - Sepsis Bundle Progress
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Cultures and sepsis labs done, antibiotics started, surgeon exam completed.
body:
**Cultures (collected 15:50, before antibiotics)**
- Blood culture set 1: peripheral, left hand.
- Blood culture set 2: left IJ central line.
- Wound swab: right chest/arm at area of drainage after cleansing.
- Tracheal aspirate.
- Urine from Foley sampling port.
All labeled and sent to the lab.

**Sepsis labs (15:55)**
Lactate 2.9 (high), WBC 18.4, Hgb 11.6, platelets 171, INR 1.4, aPTT 38, fibrinogen 380, procalcitonin 4.8. Repeat lactate ordered for 17:00; glucose 224 at 16:30.

**Antibiotics**
- Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV extended infusion (4 h) started 16:30.
- Vancomycin load 1,750 mg IV over 2 h started 16:45 via a separate lumen of the left IJ. The two drugs run on separate lumens; no co-infusion. Pharmacy (A. Chen, PharmD) verified doses (20 mg/kg load).

**Wound exam**
Dr. Okafor examined the burn wound at 16:30 with N. Ibarra, RN present and took a biopsy. Silver sulfadiazine discontinued. Mafenide acetate 5% soaks ordered, to start with the next wound care (q8h); anticipate increased pain with mafenide, so pre-medicate. OR for excision/grafting planned once he is stable.

**Hemodynamics**
16:00: T 101.2 F, HR 115, BP 104/51 (MAP 69), RR 25, SpO2 97%. 16:30: T 101.4 F, HR 116, BP 105/48 (MAP 67), RR 26, SpO2 96%. UOP 28 mL for the 1500-1600 hour (0.34 mL/kg/h). Propofol 30, fentanyl 100 mcg/h, CPOT 2/8, RASS -2. FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5, PIP 26 / Pplat 19. Feeds continue at 70 mL/h.

**Notified**
Dr. Okafor and Dr. Brandt are aware of vitals and urine output. LR 500 mL boluses ordered for 17:00 and 17:45 for MAP near 65 and low UOP; norepinephrine ordered if MAP stays below 65 after fluids.

**Plan**
Vancomycin infusing until 18:45, hourly MAP/UOP, lactate at 17:00, mafenide soaks, acetaminophen scheduled.

title: Nursing Note - Hypotension and Vasopressor Start
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: MAP fell to 64 despite boluses; norepinephrine started via central line.
body:
**Hemodynamic course**
- 16:30: HR 116, MAP 67. 17:00: HR 122, BP 105/47 (MAP 66), T 101.6 F.
- 17:15: BP 101/44 (MAP 63-64), HR 122, RR 26.
- 17:30: BP 102/45 (MAP 64), HR 121, RR 27, SpO2 95%, T 101.7 F.

**Fluid resuscitation**
LR 500 mL boluses given 17:00 and 17:45, each over 30 minutes through the left antecubital PIV, in addition to LR maintenance at 100 mL/h. MAP responded only transiently.

**Labs**
Lactate 3.8 at 17:00 (up from 2.9). Na 136, K 3.8, Mg 1.9, Phos 2.6 after replacement, Cr 1.1, BUN 27, glucose 226 (POC 227 at 17:30). Dr. Okafor and Dr. Brandt informed of MAP 64 at 17:15 and lactate 3.8.

**Norepinephrine**
Started at 17:30 at 0.05 mcg/kg/min (16 mcg/mL) via a dedicated central line lumen, double-checked with a second RN. Arterial line used for continuous MAP; titrate by 0.02-0.03 mcg/kg/min every 5-10 minutes for MAP 65 or higher. Extremities warm; right hand Doppler signals intact. Site assessed hourly for infiltration.

**Mafenide soaks**
Started 17:30 on right arm and chest after the pharmacy and surgeon confirmed; soaks cause burning pain. CPOT 2/8 with brief grimace at application; fentanyl continues at 100 mcg/h and propofol 30 mcg/kg/min. Will monitor for metabolic acidosis; ABG/BMP ordered.

**Urine output**
UOP 24 mL (1600-1700 hour; 0.29 mL/kg/h) and about 22 mL/h over the last hour; below the 30 mL/h goal. Foley patent, no kinks, no sediment. Bladder pressure remains in range.

**Respiratory**
PIP 28 / Pplat 21 at 17:30 with FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5; RT D. Alvarez, RRT aware. No new secretions.

**Family**
Jenna Whitaker and Linda Delaney updated at the bedside by Dr. Brandt with me present: infection in the bloodstream is possible, he needs medicine to support blood pressure; both tearful but asking appropriate questions.

**Plan**
Titrate norepinephrine for MAP 65 or higher, check lactate in 2 hours, continue antibiotics, hourly UOP.

title: Nursing Note - End of Shift Handoff (SBAR)
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: SBAR handoff to night RN with sepsis status, drips and pending items.
body:
**S**
Sepsis with burn wound infection, MAP supported with norepinephrine. Handoff to E. Haddad, RN at 18:50.

**B**
Hospital day 2. 22% TBSA flame burn with inhalation injury, intubated. Parkland resuscitation completed 01:30. Wound infection recognized at 14:00; cultures x4 at 15:50; pip-tazo 16:30; vancomycin 1,750 mg load 16:45 (infusing until about 18:45); LR boluses x2; norepinephrine 17:30; mafenide soaks started 17:30; silver sulfadiazine discontinued. NKDA. Full Code.

**A**
- Vitals 18:30: T 102.1 F, HR 126, BP 108/48 (MAP 68), RR 29, SpO2 94%.
- Norepinephrine 0.10 mcg/kg/min (0.05 at 17:30, 0.08 at 18:00, 0.10 at 18:30), MAP goal 65 or higher.
- Vent changed at 18:00 to set RR 18, PEEP 8, FiO2 0.50, PIP 29 / Pplat 22.
- Propofol 40 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 150 mcg/h, RASS -3.
- Insulin infusion 4 units/h, POC glucose 244 (18:30).
- UOP 20 mL (1700-1800), 0.24 mL/kg/h. Day shift (0700-1800): intake 3,786 mL, output 427 mL.
- Lactate 3.8 (17:00). ABG 18:45: pH 7.31, PaCO2 36, PaO2 92, HCO3 18, BE -8, lactate pending.
- WBC 18.4, PCT 4.8, platelets 171.
- Lines: left IJ (norepinephrine, antibiotics on separate lumens), left radial A-line, left AC PIV, Foley, OG with feeds at 70 mL/h.

**R / To do**
- Titrate norepinephrine for MAP 65 or higher; call Dr. Brandt for MAP under 65 on increasing doses or rising pressor needs.
- Follow lactate (repeat due 19:00), glucose hourly, UOP hourly; notify for UOP under 20 mL/h.
- Pending results: blood, wound, tracheal aspirate, urine cultures, wound biopsy, CBC with diff.
- Possible stress-dose steroids per intensivist if pressor needs rise.
- Mafenide soaks q8h (next 01:30), pre-medicate; watch acid-base.
- Risks: worsening shock, ARDS (PEEP 8), acute kidney injury, hyperglycemia, delirium.
- Family at bedside: Jenna and Linda updated.

title: Nursing Note - Night Shift Assessment (Sepsis Peak)
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: Night shift assessment at the height of septic shock with rising pressor needs.
body:
**Report**
Received bedside handoff from J. Morales, RN at 19:00. Allergies NKDA, Full Code, contact precautions.

**Vitals at 19:30**
T 102.4 F (peak so far), HR 133, BP 107/50 (MAP 69), RR 30, SpO2 92%. 19:00: T 102.3 F, HR 130, MAP 70.

**Cardiovascular**
Norepinephrine increased to 0.12 mcg/kg/min at 19:30 (0.10 at 19:00) via left IJ; MAP kept at 65 or higher, with the A-line transduced and zeroed at the start of the shift. Skin warm and flushed, cap refill brisk. Right hand Doppler signals intact. Lactate 4.1 at 19:00 (critical), Dr. Brandt informed.

**Respiratory**
AC/VC VT 450, RR 18 set (patient total 30), FiO2 0.50, PEEP 8. PIP 31 / Pplat 24. Suctioned for thick tan secretions with improved breath sounds. ABG 18:45: pH 7.31, PaCO2 36, PaO2 92, HCO3 18, BE -8, SaO2 94%. HOB above 30 degrees, CHG oral care due 21:00.

**Fever management**
Acetaminophen 1 g IV due 22:00; cooling measures: removed extra linens, cool washcloths to axillae/groin avoiding burn areas, room temperature lowered, no shivering seen. Temperature to bladder probe every 30 minutes.

**Neuro**
RASS -3 on propofol 40 mcg/kg/min and fentanyl 150 mcg/h, CPOT 1/8. Hydromorphone 0.5 mg given 19:15 for wound care discomfort.

**Renal / fluids**
UOP 20 mL (1800-1900 hour; 0.24 mL/kg/h); current hour tracking in the mid-20s to 30 mL, still under the 30-50 mL/h goal. LR at 100 mL/h, feeds 70 mL/h, K 3.8 at 17:00, repeat BMP at 23:00.

**Endocrine**
POC glucose 246 at 19:30. Insulin infusion 4 units/h, hourly checks.

**Infection**
Pip-tazo extended infusion until 20:30; vancomycin load done. Wound dressings (mafenide) intact, drainage on soaks. Hydrocortisone 50 mg IV planned for 20:30 per Dr. Brandt, for vasopressor-dependent shock.

**Family**
Jenna and Linda updated at bedside; they will stay until 21:00.

**Plan**
Titrate pressor, hourly labs and glucose, bundle follow-up, albumin and steroids per orders.

title: Nursing Note - Result Notification Note
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: Preliminary wound Gram stain and CBC results with bandemia reported to intensivist.
body:
**Results**
- 21:30 wound Gram stain (preliminary): many WBC, moderate Gram-positive cocci in clusters.
- CBC 21:00: WBC 21.8 (up from 18.4), 14% bands (high), segs 68%, Hgb 10.9, platelets 142 (low; down from 171).
Lab called the Gram stain result to me at 21:30 and I called Dr. Brandt immediately with read-back.

**Response**
Dr. Brandt acknowledged. Current antibiotics (vancomycin and pip-tazo) already cover Gram-positive cocci; no change ordered. Platelets will be followed on heparin SQ 5,000 units q8h; per Dr. Brandt the drop is most likely from sepsis (HIT unlikely given timing under 5 days). Dr. Okafor to be informed of the Gram stain. Final culture and sensitivity pending.

**Hydrocortisone**
Hydrocortisone 50 mg IV given at 20:30 per order (stress dose, q6h). Albumin 5% 500 mL ordered to begin at 22:00 over 4 hours.

**Vitals 21:00**
T 101.9 F, HR 124, BP 108/51 (MAP 70), RR 28, SpO2 94%. Norepinephrine 0.14 mcg/kg/min since 20:30 (0.12 at 19:30). PIP 30 / Pplat 23 on FiO2 0.50, PEEP 8.

**Endocrine**
Insulin raised to 5 units/h at 21:00; POC glucose 251 (20:30), 266 (21:30). Hourly checks.

**Renal**
UOP 28 mL (1900-2000) and 35 mL (2000-2100) = 0.34-0.43 mL/kg/h, slowly improving.

**Medications 21:00**
Chlorhexidine oral rinse, ascorbic acid, bacitracin to face, senna-docusate given per OG. Heparin SQ due 22:00.

**Infection control**
Contact precautions maintained; wound swab results documented. Family updated by phone with patient's permission.

**Plan**
Start albumin at 22:00, recheck lactate at 22:30, BMP at 23:00, titrate pressor.

title: Nursing Note - Midnight Update
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: Pressor beginning to wean, lactate clearing, urine output recovering.
body:
**Trends**
- Temperature: 101.6 F (22:00), 101.4 (23:00), 101.0 F (00:00).
- HR 120 (22:00), 117, 115 (00:00). BP 112/57 (MAP 75) at 00:00. RR 25, SpO2 96%.
- Norepinephrine reduced from 0.14 to 0.12 mcg/kg/min at 00:00 with MAP 74-75; goal MAP 65 or higher.
- Lactate 2.6 at 22:30 (from 4.1). ABG 22:30: pH 7.35, PaCO2 38, PaO2 98, HCO3 20, BE -5, SaO2 95%.
- 23:00 BMP: Na 136, K 4.0, CO2 21, BUN 29, Cr 1.3 (up from 1.1), Mg 1.9, Phos 2.7, glucose 247.

**Respiratory**
FiO2 0.50, PEEP 8, set RR 18, PIP 28 / Pplat 21. Breath sounds clearer after suctioning.

**Medications**
Hydrocortisone 50 mg given 20:30, next due 02:30. Albumin 5% 500 mL infusing since 22:00. Pip-tazo 4.5 g (extended infusion) given at 00:30. Acetaminophen 1 g IV and heparin SQ given 22:00; heparin nebulizer 23:00, albuterol 00:00.

**Urine output**
UOP 42 (2100-2200), 46 (2200-2300), 51 mL (2300-0000) = 0.62 mL/kg/h, now meeting goal. Foley patent, urine clear amber. Creatinine up, nephrotoxins (vancomycin, pip-tazo) noted; trough drawn before next vancomycin dose.

**Endocrine**
Insulin infusion down to 3 units/h at 00:00; POC glucose 241 (23:30), 225 (00:30).

**Comfort / Sedation**
RASS -3, CPOT 1/8. Propofol 40 mcg/kg/min and fentanyl 150 mcg/h. Repositioned off the burned side at 23:00; next turn due 01:00.

**Wound / Skin**
Mafenide dressings intact; next soak due 01:30 with pre-medication as needed. Skin on sacrum and heels intact.

**Plan**
Continue weaning norepinephrine as tolerated for MAP 65 or higher, ABG/lactate at 02:00, antibiotics, hourly glucose and UOP.

title: Nursing Note - Critical Result Call
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: Positive blood culture bottle called to intensivist; central line assessed.
body:
**Critical result**
At 02:40 the microbiology lab called me with a critical value: blood culture set 2 (central line), bottle 1 of 4 positive at 10 hours, Gram-positive cocci in clusters. Read back verified. I notified Dr. Brandt at 02:45.

**Response**
Dr. Brandt acknowledged. Continue vancomycin (next dose 04:30, pharmacy to follow level) and pip-tazo; identification and sensitivities pending. Peripheral set and other bottles still in process. Continue to wean norepinephrine for MAP 65 or higher, vancomycin trough before 04:30 dose, labs at 05:00, repeat cultures per team.

title: Nursing Note - Norepinephrine Off
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: Pressor weaned off at 04:30 with MAP stable; vancomycin dosing and level documented.
body:

Level drawn at 04:15 before the 04:30 dose: 11.6 mcg/mL. Dose of 1,250 mg started 04:30 over 2 hours via a dedicated lumen. Pharmacy aware of the level and creatinine trend. Pip-tazo next dose 08:30.

Creatinine 1.1 (17:00 Tue) to 1.3 (23:00); AM creatinine drawn with the 05:00 labs, results pending. UOP 63 mL (0300-0400), 0.77 mL/kg/h. BUN 29 at 23:00. Avoid additional nephrotoxins; monitor for a rise.

ABG 04:00: pH 7.38, PaCO2 39, PaO2 104, HCO3 22, BE -2. Procalcitonin 9.6 at 04:00 (4.8 at 15:55). Lactate 1.8 at 02:00. Platelets 142 (21:00). 05:00 labs pending.

Propofol reduced to 30 mcg/kg/min and fentanyl 100 mcg/h at 04:00; RASS -2, CPOT 1/8.

Monitor MAP off pressor, labs at 05:00 and CXR, continue antibiotics, SAT/SBT at 08:00 with day team.

title: Nursing Note - Night Shift Handoff (SBAR)
author: E. Haddad, RN

body:

title: Nursing Note - Day Shift Assessment
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Day shift assessment, patient off pressors and improving.
body:

AC/VC 450 x 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.40, PIP 24 / Pplat 17, SpO2 98%, RR 17. Coarse breath sounds, scant thin secretions. ETT 24 cm at teeth. Heparin neb given 07:00; albuterol 08:00 due.

05:00: WBC 19.2, bands 9%, Hgb 10.4, platelets 128 on heparin SQ, lactate 1.5. Procalcitonin 9.6 at 04:00. Central line culture bottle positive (GPC in clusters) at 02:40; on vancomycin and pip-tazo; vancomycin level 11.6.

Mafenide dressings to right arm and chest intact, minimal drainage, no new spreading erythema along the marked line. Face with bacitracin. Turn q2h on low air-loss mattress.

Left IJ day 3 clean, dry and intact; left AC PIV; Foley; OG.

Linda at bedside; Jenna expected later.

SAT/SBT, labs, mafenide soak at 09:30, hydrocortisone and pip-tazo at 08:30.

title: Nursing Note - SAT Passed
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Sedation interruption passed; patient awake and ready for SBT.
body:
**SAT 08:00**
Propofol turned off at 08:00 per order; fentanyl 100 mcg/h continued. Pre-SAT: RASS -2, HR 97, BP 111/60 (MAP 77), SpO2 98%, T 99.8 F.

**Response**
- Awake within 10 minutes, RASS 0, calm, makes eye contact.
- Follows commands: squeezes left hand, wiggles toes, nods yes/no appropriately.
- CPOT 0/8 at rest; no grimacing.
- Hemodynamics stable (HR 90s, MAP 76-78), RR 17-18 on AC/VC, no dyssynchrony.
- Attentive, oriented by nodding to name and hospital; CAM-ICU negative.
- Mouthed "water"; mouth swabs and oral care provided.
- Family: Linda at bedside, reassured; he squeezed her hand.

**SBT readiness**
FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5, no pressor since 04:30, PIP 23 / Pplat 16, lactate 1.5. SBT ordered and planned for 09:30 with RT D. Alvarez, RRT, with an ABG and cuff leak test; plan is to wean FiO2 to 0.35 for the trial. Pass criteria: RR under 30, SpO2 92% or higher, HR change under 20%, RSBI under 105.

**Stool**
One loose stool at 02:00 related to tube feeds, small volume. The 09:00 senna-docusate dose will be held for loose stool; bowel regimen reevaluated. Stool recorded; C. diff testing not required (fewer than 3 stools).

**Other**
Pip-tazo and hydrocortisone due 08:30. POC glucose 169 (07:30). UOP 70 mL (0700-0800) = 0.85 mL/kg/h. Insulin infusion 1 unit/h at 08:00. Left wrist restraint remains until extubation.

**Plan**
SBT at 09:30 with RT; extubation if passed and cuff leak present; keep NPO. Dexmedetomidine to be considered after extubation for anxiety.

title: Nursing Note - Extubation
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: SBT passed and patient extubated; post-extubation assessment and dexmedetomidine started.
body:
**SBT**
Done 09:30 on PS 5 / PEEP 5, FiO2 0.35 for 30 minutes with RT D. Alvarez, RRT: RSBI 58, RR under 30, SpO2 98-99%, HR stable, no distress, cuff leak present. ABG 09:00: pH 7.40, PaCO2 40, PaO2 96, HCO3 24.

**Extubation 10:45**
Feeds stopped at 10:30, OG suctioned. Fentanyl infusion stopped at 10:45. Dr. Brandt present; oral and ETT suction, cuff deflated, ETT removed at 10:45 on a deep breath with cough. Nasal cannula 4 L/min applied.

**Post-extubation assessment**
- 10:50: HR 95, BP 112/61 (MAP 78), RR 20, SpO2 97%, T 99.7 F. 11:00: RR 22, SpO2 96%. 11:15: HR 91, RR 23, SpO2 96%.
- Voice hoarse, expected after intubation. No stridor, no drooling, cough effective, clearing thin secretions with suction.
- Breath sounds clear to coarse, equal and bilateral. Pain 4/10 (sore throat).
- RASS 0, calm, alert, following commands.
- Soft left wrist restraint removed at extubation; skin intact.

**Dexmedetomidine**
Started at 11:00 at 0.4 mcg/kg/h for anxiety; propofol off since 08:00. HR and BP monitored; hold for HR under 50 or MAP under 65.

**OG removal**
OG tube removed at 11:15. Nostril and oropharynx without bleeding. NPO until the bedside swallow screen; oral care with swabs. HOB above 30 degrees, aspiration and fall precautions initiated.

**I&O**
UOP 70 (0900-1000), 72 mL (1000-1100) = 0.85-0.88 mL/kg/h. LR 75 mL/h. POC glucose 154 (10:30), 150 (11:30); insulin 1 unit/h.

**Plan**
Incentive spirometry hourly, cough and deep breathing, wean O2 for SpO2 92% or higher, ABG at 12:00, ondansetron if nauseated.

title: Nursing Note - Post-Extubation Update
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Post-extubation nausea treated, pain numeric, early mobility and family visit.
body:

Nasal cannula 4 L/min. 12:00: SpO2 96%, RR 23, HR 91, BP 113/62 (MAP 79), T 99.6 F. ABG 12:00 on 4 L NC: pH 7.39, PaCO2 41, PaO2 88, HCO3 24, SaO2 96%. Incentive spirometry coached hourly to about 1,000 mL, cough productive of small amount of clear sputum. Voice still hoarse; no stridor.

Reported nausea at about 12:15; no emesis. Ondansetron 4 mg IV given 12:30. Repositioned upright, sips not allowed (NPO until swallow screen at 16:00), oral care done. Nausea improving at 12:45.

Pain scores now numeric: 4/10 (throat and right arm), CPOT discontinued. RASS 0. Dexmedetomidine 0.4 mcg/kg/h since 11:00, no bradycardia. CAM-ICU negative at 12:00. Acetaminophen 1 g IV q8h scheduled, next 14:00.

Insulin infusion stopped at 12:00; correction scale lispro per order. POC glucose 150 (11:30). Next check at 12:30.

UOP 71 mL (1100-1200) = 0.87 mL/kg/h. LR decreased to 50 mL/h at 12:00.

**Mobility**
Order for out of bed to chair with PT/OT and nursing from 12:00; dangle and chair planned with 2 assist after the 14:00 dressing change. Bed alarm on, call light within reach, non-skid socks, fall precautions.

Jenna Whitaker and Linda visited; Ava (age 6) saw him by video call, he smiled and waved with his left hand. Family teary and happy.

Swallow screen 16:00, wean O2, dressing change 14:00, pre-medicate before dressing change.

title: Nursing Note - Dressing Change
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Mafenide dressing change with improving wound appearance and controlled but significant pain.
body:
**Pre-medication**

- Drainage markedly decreased, thin serosanguineous, no purulence, odor much reduced.

title: Nursing Note - Culture Results and Swallow Screen
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: MSSA bacteremia identified, antibiotic changes, swallow screen passed, oxycodone started.
body:
**Swallow screen**
Bedside swallow screen done at 16:00: alert, upright 90 degrees, voice hoarse but improving, 3 oz water test passed without cough, wet voice or desaturation. Diet advanced per order; soft diet with high-protein supplements to begin at 18:00 (dietitian following). Aspiration precautions maintained.

At 15:00 the lab called blood culture results: MSSA in 2 of 4 bottles (one peripheral, one central line). Tracheal aspirate: normal flora. Urine culture no growth at 24 hours. Procalcitonin 6.1 at 16:00 (9.6 earlier). Called to Dr. Brandt at 15:00.

Dr. Raman (Infectious Disease) saw the patient at 11:00 and followed along; after MSSA was identified at 15:00 the recommendation is narrowing to cefazolin. Vancomycin stopped at 15:30. Repeat blood cultures x2 (peripheral and central line) drawn at 16:00 before the next antibiotic dose.

Left IJ stays for now; ID will have it removed if repeat cultures turn positive. Site clean, dry, intact.

Pain 4/10 at 16:00. Oxycodone 5 mg PO given at 16:45 after swallow screen. Acetaminophen IV scheduled.

**Vitals 16:00**
T 99.3 F, HR 90, BP 112/64 (MAP 80), RR 20, SpO2 96% on 2 L NC (weaned from 4 L). Dexmedetomidine 0.4 mcg/kg/h. UOP 69 mL (1500-1600) = 0.84 mL/kg/h.

Out of bed to chair with PT/OT at 15:20 with 2 assist, tolerated 20 minutes, SpO2 95-96%.

Remove left AC PIV at 18:00, stop LR then, saline carrier via central line, soft diet 18:00, labs at 17:00, continue to monitor.

title: Nursing Note - Pain and Sleep

title: Nursing Note - Line and Tube Removal

body:
